item.title: Bayesian Optimization Reduces Car Drag by 6.5% Using LES
item.description: This paper investigates passive control for drag reduction on a simplified road vehicle geometry, specifically the square-back Windsor body, through…
item.content:encoded:
Type: 🤖 ML/Aerodynamics | Relevance: 40/100

This paper investigates passive control for drag reduction on a simplified road vehicle geometry, specifically the square-back Windsor body, through the optimization of a rear roof extension. The study employs high-fidelity wall-resolved large eddy simulation (LES) to model the flow. The optimization process relies on Gaussian process-based surrogate modeling combined with Bayesian optimization, guided by an expected improvement criterion, to efficiently explore the design space defined by the roof extension’s taper penetration distance, angle of incidence, and length.

The optimization converged within six iterations, requiring a total of 60 LES simulations, and resulted in a 6.5% reduction in drag. The authors identified six distinct mechanisms contributing to this drag reduction, including diffuser-induced pressure recovery, base-size reduction, and modifications to the vertical wake balance. The optimal configuration was found when the roof extension angle corresponded to the onset of separation, with both the taper penetration distance and extension length at their maximum values within the analyzed domain.

This work provides a framework for aerodynamic optimization, demonstrating how coupled wake–geometry interactions can be effectively managed for improved aerodynamic performance. While the application is to road vehicles, the methodology of using Gaussian processes for design optimization with high-fidelity CFD is relevant to broader engineering design challenges.

Reference

  1. Kacper Janczuk, Adrian Gaylard, Aimee S. Morgans, “Bayesian optimisation of a roof extension/spoiler on a simplified vehicle, employing wall-resolved large eddy simulation,” Journal of Fluid Mechanics, 2026-03-09. Link

item.title: Machine Learning for Mars Rotorcraft: Faster Aerodynamic Design and Optimization
item.description: This paper describes a methodology for optimizing the design of a long-range Mars rotorcraft by integrating high-fidelity simulation data with…
item.content:encoded:
Type: 🤖 ML/Aerodynamics | Relevance: 40/100

This paper describes a methodology for optimizing the design of a long-range Mars rotorcraft by integrating high-fidelity simulation data with machine learning techniques. The approach begins with generating extensive aerodynamic simulation databases for a hex-rotor bi-plane tailsitter aircraft across various geometric perturbations and flight conditions. Over 3,000 full aircraft aerodynamic simulations were performed using GPU-enabled OVERFLOW with an actuator disk model, taking approximately 1.5 weeks on 32 GPU nodes equipped with 128 NVIDIA V100 GPUs.

Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), sparse GPRs, and various Neural Networks were then trained as surrogate models to predict airfoil and airframe aerodynamic performance based on flight conditions, airframe geometry, and rotor control inputs. These surrogate models, combined with additional modules for aircraft mass and inertia, enabled another 3,000 aircraft simulations in CAMRAD-II in less than six hours using 240 CPU cores. This significantly reduced the computational cost for subsequent design iterations. The framework was then configured for simultaneous optimization of aircraft parameters and flight conditions, aiming for objectives such as maximum range or endurance while satisfying controllability constraints.

This work demonstrates a practical application of data-driven methods to bring higher-fidelity simulation data into the early stages of conceptual design. By creating accurate and efficient surrogate models, the design process can achieve improved accuracy and potentially identify critical design issues much earlier than traditional methods, despite the computational expense of the initial high-fidelity data generation.

This paper review was generated by Gemini 2.5 Flash and curated by AeroSentinel v2.5.0.

Reference

  1. , “Long-Range Mars Rotorcraft Design Optimization using Machine Learning,” NASA Technical Report, Unknown. Link
